extracted.intended_audience: researchers, journalists, fact-checkers, platform moderators, and readers tracking fake-news websites
extracted.subtask_description: A catalog-style reference listing websites tied to misinformation, impersonation, plagiarism, coordinated networks, malware, and other behaviors used to classify sites as fake or untrustworthy. Useful for monitoring, research, and moderation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impostor site / imitates legitimate outlet
rubrics_metrics.description: Impostor site, per PolitiFact / Imitates [legitimate outlet].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sites that mimic the branding, name, or domain of established news organizations (e.g., washinqtonpost.com, usatosday.com, usanetwork.info, Fox-news24.com) to appear legitimate. Often noted by fact-checkers as 'impostor site' or 'spoof' and may plagiarize or republish content to bolster credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fabricated stories and fabricated quotes
rubrics_metrics.description: Fabricated a story with quotes from fictitious persons / fabricated quotes or statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contains wholly invented narratives or quotations presented as factual (example: 'Fabricated a story with quotes from fictitious persons'). Fact-checkers flag these as fabrication rather than misinterpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Published false stories / hoaxes
rubrics_metrics.description: Published false story about a public figure or event / circulated hoaxes (death hoaxes, false election claims, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes false claims about public figures (e.g., false stories about Nancy Pelosi, false claim that Trump made an announcement on a given date), death hoaxes, or broad fabricated narratives that have been debunked by multiple sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copied / plagiarized content (including from satire/parody and other fake sites)
rubrics_metrics.description: Copied article from The People's Cube / The Last Line of Defense / Empire News / parody sites such as The Postillon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Republishing verbatim or lightly edited content from satire, parody, or other dubious outlets while presenting it as genuine news; also includes plagiarism of mainstream outlets' content or copying site footers/metadata to simulate legitimacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sourced claims from fringe online communities
rubrics_metrics.description: Sourced a false claim from /r/The_Donald or similar fringe forums.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Articles that take claims originating in fringe message boards, subreddits, or closed communities and present them as verified facts. Fact-checkers note the original provenance (e.g., Reddit) as evidence of low credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spread COVID-19 misinformation (cures, vaccines, unproven claims)
rubrics_metrics.description: Spread false claims about cures for COVID-19; spread misinformation about COVID-19 vaccines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims about miracle cures, false safety/efficacy statements about vaccines, or other health-related misinformation flagged by fact-checkers and health authorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promotes conspiracy theories and extremist narratives
rubrics_metrics.description: Promotes QAnon, Holocaust denial, anti-Ukrainian disinformation, misogynistic or anti-democratic narratives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sites repeatedly publishing or amplifying organized conspiracy theories or extremist content (e.g., QAnon), as identified by fact-checkers and monitoring organizations (Graphika, Global Disinformation Index, Center for Countering Digital Hate).

rubrics_metrics.name: Manipulated or misattributed media as evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Used Photoshopped image as evidence / manipulated and misattributed celebrity quote.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of doctored images, fabricated documents, or quotes attributed to people who did not say them; often presented as 'proof' in support of false claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affiliated with coordinated inauthentic behavior or spam networks
rubrics_metrics.description: Sites tied to spam networks or coordinated inauthentic behavior (e.g., networks taken down by Facebook in Myanmar; Macedonian/Georgian networks during 2016 election).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Groups of websites sharing ownership, infrastructure, or operational patterns used to push coordinated narratives, often for profit or political influence; may be removed or flagged by platforms for CIB.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shared infrastructure / metadata signals
rubrics_metrics.description: Shares the same IP address or ad network ID or website metadata with other known fake sites.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical indicators (shared IPs, ad IDs, identical site metadata) used to link sites into networks or attribute shared ownership/operation; cited as evidence in the catalog (e.g., 'Shares the same IP address or ad network ID as departed.co').

rubrics_metrics.name: Monetized for profit / ad-driven motives
rubrics_metrics.description: Registered for profit motives and monetized via ad revenue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sites created primarily to generate ad revenue or other profit (clickbait, sensational false stories, impersonators) rather than to inform; examples include networks set up around the 2016 US election for profit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attempts to install malware or harvest personal data
rubrics_metrics.description: Part of network that posted death hoaxes to spread malware; contains pop-up that asks for personal information; reportedly attempts to install malware.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sites that deploy malicious technical behavior (malware downloads, deceptive pop-ups requesting personal info) in addition to or instead of misinformation; flagged by platform takedowns and press reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article spinning / low-quality automated rewriting
rubrics_metrics.description: Accused of using article spinning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Automatically or mechanically altered copies of articles that degrade quality and obscure original sourcing; an indicator of low editorial standards and deceptive republishing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Republishing or repeating false claims from other dubious sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Republished a hoax about Barack Obama on a $1 bill; reposted false stories from Christian Times Newspaper or World News Daily Report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sites that amplify existing hoaxes or false claims by republishing them without verification, contributing to wider circulation of misinformation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plagiarizes or syndicates mainstream outlet content deceptively
rubrics_metrics.description: Plagiarizes CNBC stories or copies footers/formatting to appear authoritative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Direct copying of mainstream media content or site elements to create the impression of legitimacy while potentially mixing plagiarized mainstream content with false or misleading material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uses fabricated documents or letters to support claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Fabricated a letter from the British Ministry of Defense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presentation of forged documents, fake official communications, or invented 'insider' letters as corroborating evidence for false narratives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flagged by multiple fact-checkers and monitoring organizations
rubrics_metrics.description: Per PolitiFact / Per FactCheck.org / noted by Graphika and NewsGuard / flagged by Snopes, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Repeated identification by reputable fact-checking organizations and research monitors is used as a signal of a site's unreliability; entries commonly cite these sources as justification for inclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amplified or shared by public figures (indicator of reach)
rubrics_metrics.description: Shared by Paul Gosar in his newsletter in 2023 / amplified by politicians or influencers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When elected officials or high-profile figures republish or link to a site, it is noted as an amplification vector and evidence of impact, though not proof of veracity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Associated with extremist actors or illegal behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: Site founders or operators linked to arrests, carrying weapons during vote tally, or meeting with extremist groups (e.g., Proud Boys).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational ties between site personnel and extremist or violent actors (arrests, known affiliations) are used as context for assessing a site's credibility and risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copies satire/parody content and presents it as real
rubrics_metrics.description: Copied story from The Postillon / copied article from a parody/satire site and presented without satire context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguishes intentional deception from humorous content: republishing satire as factual news is treated as misinformation when the source/context is removed or misrepresented.
